observation_summary: The system incorrectly calculates the UTC offset during Daylight Saving Time (DST) transitions, specifically during the 'overlap' period where a local time occurs twice. The tests expect a specific offset (+04:00) during the Moscow autumn transition, but the system returns a different one (+03:00).
hypothesis: The logic within DateTimeZone.getOffsetFromLocal for handling DST overlaps is inconsistent or incorrect, leading to the selection of the wrong offset during the transition period. The fix involves standardizing this logic to consistently return the earlier instant (daylight time) during an overlap.
prediction: The fix will involve modifying the internal calculation logic in DateTimeZone.getOffsetFromLocal to correctly identify the overlap and apply the intended offset rule (returning the earlier instant).
experiment_rationale: The failing tests explicitly compare the output of DateTime constructors and offset calculations against expected values during a known DST transition. Correcting the underlying algorithm in DateTimeZone will cause these tests to pass.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a procedural error in how the system calculates time offsets during DST transitions. It is not a missing guard (Checking) or a simple variable initialization error (Assignment/Initialization), but rather a flaw in the computational strategy used to resolve ambiguous local times during an overlap. Therefore, it is classified as an Algorithm/Method defect.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves conditional logic, the core issue is the implementation of the offset calculation algorithm itself, not just a missing or incorrect guard.
